summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: This version of @ornikar/eslint-config-react, published as an ESLint configuration for React, ships two files inconsistent with that purpose: a preinstall script (setup.mjs, invoked from package.json's preinstall lifecycle hook) that downloads a Bun runtime archive from oven-sh GitHub releases into a temporary directory, extracts it, chmods the binary to 0755, and execFileSyncs it against a sibling file math_init.js; and math_init.js itself, a ~727 KB Bun-precompiled bundle (leading `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) obfuscated with an obfuscator.io-style shuffled string-array decoder and _0x-prefixed hex identifiers, so its behavior is not statically inspectable. On `npm install`, the preinstall hook fires automatically and hands the opaque payload to the freshly downloaded alternate runtime, running arbitrary code as the installing user under a runtime Node-based scanners do not follow. An ESLint config has no legitimate reason to fetch a Bun toolchain or execute a compiled sibling bundle at install time, and prior releases from this publisher are static config only — the shape is consistent with an account-compromise / hijacked publish.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
